### Summary

### Summary

`uv run <entrypoint>` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` because `uv` marks local editable workspace packages as "already installed" even when the site-packages `.pth` link fails to resolve the root module. Re-saving `pyproject.toml` updates the timestamp, forcing `uv` to rebuild/reinstall the package, which temporarily fixes the error until the next environment state check.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Initialize a package with `uv init` (using a `src/` layout).
2. Run `uv run <project_name>`.
3. The entrypoint script inside `.venv/bin/<project_name>` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '<project_name>'` because `uv` reports `Requirement already installed: package==0.1.0`.
4. Re-save `pyproject.toml` (e.g., `touch pyproject.toml`).
5. Run `uv run <project_name>` again. `uv` detects `Requirement installed, but not fresh`, rebuilds/reinstalls the wheel, and execution succeeds.

### Verbose Logs

<details>
<summary>Logs showing failure vs recovery after saving pyproject.toml</summary>

```text

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/rakshitsingh25/Desktop/work/.venv/bin/work", line 4, in <module>
    from work import main
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'work'

# After re-saving pyproject.toml:
DEBUG Requirement installed, but not fresh: work==0.1.0 (from file:///Users/rakshitsingh25/Desktop/work)
Building work @ file:///Users/rakshitsingh25/Desktop/work
Installed 1 package in 3ms
Hello from work!

macOS
